policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders no separate quantifier in 'whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning', but a resumptive πάντα after ὅσα is pleonastic and is absorbed by 'whatsoever things'; the English neither requires nor excludes it. Sole note is alternative_rendering (stedfastness) and cannot decide a reading.

ASV distinguishes the two verbs: the first is 'were written aforetime' (προεγράφη), the second plain 'were written' with no second 'aforetime', which is the simplex ἐγράφη and not RP's repeated προεγράφη.
ASV reads 'according to Christ Jesus', the order Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν; ASV keeps the order of the two names in this title pair, so 'Jesus Christ' would be expected for Treg.
ASV text reads 'Christ also received you' (ὑμᾶς), and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read us.' puts ἡμᾶς in the margin, confirming the second person stands in the text.

Presence or absence of the article before θεοῦ is not expressible in English: ASV's 'to the glory of God' renders either. The verse's textual note concerns you/us in the previous clause, not this unit.
ASV opens the verse 'For I say', a causal connective rendering γάρ; RP's δέ would be rendered 'Now' or 'But'.
ASV reads 'that Christ hath been made a minister' with no second name; the added Ἰησοῦν of RP would appear as 'Christ Jesus', and a proper name cannot be absorbed silently.
ASV's 'hath been made a minister' is a perfect, rendering the perfect infinitive γεγενῆσθαι; Treg's aorist γένεσθαι would give 'was made' / 'became'.

English imperative syntax fixes 'Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles' whatever the Greek order, since the vocative cannot stand between verb and object in ASV idiom; and r00-base/r01 differ only in punctuation, which the English cannot show.
ASV reads 'And let all the peoples praise him', a third person imperative rendering ἐπαινεσάτωσαν; RP's second person ἐπαινέσατε would give 'praise ye him' as in the first line.
The article before πάσης γνώσεως is not distinguishable in ASV's 'filled with all knowledge'; both readings yield the same English.
ASV reads 'able also to admonish one another', the reciprocal ἀλλήλους; RP's ἄλλους would be 'others'.
τολμηρότερον and τολμηροτέρως are comparative adverbial forms of the same word and both are rendered 'the more boldly'; ASV cannot distinguish them.
ASV reads 'I write the more boldly unto you in some measure' with no vocative; RP's added ἀδελφοί would appear as 'brethren', which ASV renders wherever it stands (as in v. 14).
ὑπό and ἀπό with the agent are both rendered 'of God' in ASV's 'the grace that was given me of God'; the English does not distinguish the preposition.
ASV reads 'a minister of Christ Jesus', the order Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ; RP's Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ would give 'Jesus Christ'.
ASV's 'I have therefore my glorying' can render the articular τὴν καύχησιν or the anarthrous noun, since the possessive 'my' is supplied from the context either way.
The order of τι and λαλεῖν is not recoverable from 'I will not dare to speak of any things'; English fixes verb before object regardless.

ASV text reads 'the power of the Holy Spirit' (πνεύματος ἁγίου), and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read the Spirit of God. One reads the Spirit.' relegates θεοῦ and the bare πνεύματος to the margin.

ASV continues the participial chain with 'yea, making it my aim so to preach the gospel', a participle rendering φιλοτιμούμενον; Treg's finite φιλοτιμοῦμαι would start a new main clause ('I make it my aim').

ASV must front the verb in 'They shall see, to whom no tidings of him came' because the headless relative cannot precede its verb in English, so the order does not report the Greek; r00-base and r01 differ only in how the same words are displayed.
ASV reads 'having these many years a longing', and 'many' renders πολλῶν; ASV renders ἱκανός of time as 'long' (e.g. 'of long time', 'a long time'), not 'many'.
ἄν and ἐάν with the subjunctive here are the same particle orthographically varied; both are rendered 'whensoever'.
ASV's sentence breaks off unfinished after 'Spain' into the parenthesis and closes with a dash; RP's added ἐλεύσομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς would supply the apodosis 'I will come to you', which ASV does not have.
ASV's 'and their debtors they are' fixes its own emphatic English order; the relative order of εἰσίν and αὐτῶν is not recoverable from it.
The article with the place name is not shown in English: 'unto Spain' renders εἰς Σπανίαν and εἰς τὴν Σπανίαν alike.
ASV reads 'in the fulness of the blessing of Christ'; RP's added τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τοῦ would give 'the blessing of the gospel of Christ', and ASV has no 'gospel' here.

ASV's 'and that my ministration ... may be acceptable' repeats the 'that' of the first purpose clause as English requires for a second coordinated subjunctive, so it does not show whether a second ἵνα stood in the Greek.
ASV's 'may be acceptable to the saints' places the verb before the dative as English demands; the Greek order of τοῖς ἁγίοις and γένηται is not recoverable.

ASV's 'that I may come unto you in joy ... and together with you find rest' is the routine English resolution of a circumstantial participle into a coordinate finite verb, so it does not distinguish the participle ἐλθών from the subjunctive ἔλθω.

The 'and' before 'together with you find rest' is required by ASV's coordination of the two verbs and would appear whether or not καί stood in the Greek; it is tied to the unresolved ἐλθών/ἔλθω question in the same clause.
